| County | Tornadoes 1950‑2000 (climate.met.psu.edu) | 2023 median household income (census.gov / ACS) | 2020 population (census.gov) | Meets all criteria? |
|--------|--------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Cameron** | 3 tornadoes | **$47,681** | 4,547 | **Yes** |
| **Forest** | 7 tornadoes | **$48,084** | 6,973 | **Yes** |
| **Sullivan** | 10 tornadoes | $69,764 | 5,840 | No – income > $49k |
| **Potter** | 6 tornadoes | $59,840 | 16,396 | No – income > $49k |
| **Fulton** | 1 tornado | $65,836 | 14,556 | No – < 3 tornadoes |

**Which counties satisfy all three conditions?**  
**Cameron County** and **Forest County**.

---

### Sources

1. **Number of tornadoes (1950‑2000)** – the table in the “PA Extreme Weather – Tornado” page on climate.met.psu.edu lists the counts per county and shows:
   * *Cameron – 3*, *Forest – 7*【source: climate.met.psu.edu table excerpt】.

2. **2023 median household income** – ACS 2023 estimates (converted to 2024 dollars where noted) show:
   * *Cameron — $47,681*【source: Countypulse (Cameron)】.
   * *Forest — $48,084*【source: Countypulse (Forest) or FRED series MHIPA42053A052NCEN】.

3. **Most‑recent population ranking (2020)** – the Wikipedia “Least populated counties in Pennsylvania” list (directly derived from the 2020 Census) identifies the five smallest counties:
   * *Cameron — 4,547*
   * *Sullivan — 5,840*
   * *Forest — 6,973*
   * *Fulton — 14,556*
   * *Potter — 16,396*【source: Wikipedia: Least populated counties in Pennsylvania】.

---

### How the criteria are met

| County | ≥ 3 tornadoes? | Median income < $49k? | 2020 population among the five smallest? |
|--------|----------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Cameron | Yes (3) | Yes ($47,681) | Yes (rank 1) |
| Forest  | Yes (7) | Yes ($48,084) | Yes (rank 3) |
| Sullivan | Yes (10) | **No** | Yes |
| Potter | Yes (6) | **No** | Yes (rank 5) |
| Fulton | **No** (1) | **No** | Yes (rank 4) |

Only Cameron and Forest satisfy **all three** conditions simultaneously.

**Conclusion**: Cameron County and Forest County are the only Pennsylvania counties that had at least three tornadoes from 1950‑2000, had a 2023 median household income below $49,000 (in 2023 dollars), and are among the five least‑populated counties in Pennsylvania according to the 2020 Census.

**Cameron County** is a county in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. As of the 2020 census, the population was 4,547,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-3) making it Pennsylvania's least populous county. Its county seat is Emporium.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR6-4) The county was created on March 29, 1860, from parts of Clinton, Elk, McKean, and Potter counties. It is named for Senator Simon Cameron. The county is part of the North Central region of the commonwealth.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-5)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 398.4 square miles (1,032 km 2), of which 396.2 square miles (1,026 km 2) is land and 2.2 square miles (5.7 km 2) (0.5%) is water.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR1-6) It has a warm-summer humid continental climate (_Dfb_) and average monthly temperatures in Emporium range from 24.2°F in January to 69.3°F in July, while in Driftwood they range from 24.9°F in January to 69.9°F in July.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-7)
*   McKean County (north)  
*   Potter County (northeast)  
*   Clinton County (east)  
*   Clearfield County (south)  
*   Elk County (west)
Cameron County is the only county in the state of Pennsylvania to not be crossed by either an interstate or U.S. Route.
